steps.title: Welcome — and thank you!
steps.text: Thanks for signing up for Campaignia. This is your home base; here is a quick tour of the essentials.

steps.title: Finding your way
steps.text: I know there isn't much here yet, but this is how you navigate in and out of your screens.

steps.title: Start a {campaign}
steps.text: Click here to create your first {campaign} — the world your {sessions} and graphic novel live inside. Once you have one, its tile gets a Details button — that is where its image, Lore / Background, and member settings live.

steps.title: Your tokens
steps.text: This is your token balance. Generating images spends tokens; click here anytime to top up.

steps.title: Need a hand? Just ask
steps.text: Tap the ?s button any time to ask us anything about Campaignia - we'll point you to the right spot.

steps.title: Your profile
steps.text: Open this for your account details, plan and tokens — and to sign out.

steps.title: Stuck? Ask us
steps.text: Open this anytime for quick answers about how Campaignia works.

steps.title: Edit your {campaign}
steps.text: Click the pencil to rename your {campaign} or update its description anytime — and to write your {campaign}'s Lore / Background: the backstory and world it all takes place in.

steps.title: Invite members
steps.text: Invite others to join your {campaign} — give them a character to manage, or simply let them follow along. Each member can even build their own version of the story.

steps.title: Your cast
steps.text: Add the characters in your {campaign} here, with reference images so their likeness stays consistent across every panel.

steps.title: Add a {session}
steps.text: Start a new {session} and paste your story, transcript, notes, whatever you have — Campaignia turns it into an illustrated storyboard, ready to publish.

steps.title: Asset Library
steps.text: Upload maps, locations, items, or artwork for Campaignia to use as references across your {sessions} — it helps lock in the look you want and keep your images consistent.

steps.title: Archives
steps.text: Images you save are kept here to reuse later — swap them into any panel, or publish one to the public Library to show off a little.

steps.title: Publish your story
steps.text: When your {sessions} are ready, turn your work into a shareable graphic novel — or order a printed book.

steps.title: Name your character
steps.text: Give your character a name — add a nickname after a slash (like 'Theron / Ash') and Campaignia will recognize both.

steps.title: Player name
steps.text: Working from a transcript? Add the player's real name so Campaignia can tell who's speaking in the log.

steps.title: Visual & personality traits
steps.text: Describe how they look and act — appearance, clothing, temperament, mannerisms. The more you give here, the better Campaignia captures them.

steps.title: Reference images
steps.text: Have pictures, drawings, or renderings of your character? Add them here. No images? No problem — Campaignia will create one for you.

steps.title: Create your character
steps.text: Click Create, then follow the on-screen instructions for building your reference image. These references stay style-neutral on purpose, so your character looks right in any art style.

steps.title: Your characters
steps.text: These are your {campaign} characters — the canonical version of each one. Their reference image and prompt are reused across every {session}, so they stay consistent.

steps.title: Add a character
steps.text: Add a new character here — give them a name, a description, and any reference pictures you have.

steps.title: Refine a character
steps.text: Click a character to view or refine them. This is their canonical look, used across the whole {campaign}.

steps.title: Your asset library
steps.text: Just like characters, assets give Campaignia visual references — locations, NPCs (people), and items it can pull into your panels to keep your world consistent.

steps.title: Add an asset
steps.text: Add a location, NPC, or item here that you want to appear consistently across your story.

steps.title: Name & keywords
steps.text: Name your asset — it can have several. Separate them with a slash and Campaignia will match any of them when they come up in your story.

steps.title: Category
steps.text: Tag it as a Location, NPC, or Item. Locations double as references for your scene backgrounds.

steps.title: Describe it
steps.text: Write what this asset looks like and Campaignia can generate a reference image from it — or leave it blank and upload your own. You can edit this description anytime.

steps.title: Generate or upload
steps.text: Generate an image from your description, or upload one. Once it's there you can Retouch it, Regenerate a fresh take, Revert your last change, or Replace it with an image from your Archive.

steps.title: Your archive
steps.text: Any image you generate in Campaignia can be archived. This is where you find them all — reuse them in your story, or publish one to the public Library to share with the world.

steps.title: Publish your story
steps.text: When your story is ready, this is where you publish it.

steps.title: Whose version?
steps.text: Choose whose version you want to publish — your version, or one of your members' versions.

steps.title: Include in print
steps.text: Tick the box for each {session} you want in the book.

steps.title: Preview & Export
steps.text: Switch here to set up and preview your book before you publish.

steps.title: Title
steps.text: Give your book a title. Each version keeps its own.

steps.title: Cover, back and title images
steps.text: Set these from your Archive. The × on a tile removes that picture, and the tiles show you the crop the printed page will use. Clear the cover and you get a plain framed cover instead.

steps.title: Draw your title
steps.text: Have your title drawn as artwork instead of set in type. It costs a token, and it goes to your Archive so you can put it back later.

steps.title: Layout
steps.text: Comic, picture book, or magazine.

steps.title: Optimize
steps.text: When the look is right, this takes you to Optimize — the last step before you publish or order.

steps.title: Optimize
steps.text: Here your book is prepared for printing: page breaks, decorations, and how each page is laid out.

steps.title: The AI layout review
steps.text: Our AI engine reads your book the way an editor would — looking for errors, flow and density — and fixes what it finds to make the best book it can. It costs tokens, and it tells you how many before it starts.

steps.title: Order & Publish
steps.text: The last stop.

steps.title: Order a printed copy
steps.text: Make your selections here, then prepare and approve your book for printing. The options vary with your page count.

steps.title: Publish to the Library
steps.text: Publish your book as a shareable web page.

steps.title: Where your story lives
steps.text: This is where your story lives — the heart of a session.

steps.title: Your story
steps.text: This is your story. Whatever you have — an actual story, a transcript, journal entries, session notes — we'll take it and use it. This is also the one field owned by the Story Master — if you've joined a campaign as a member, you'll be able to read it but not edit it.

steps.title: Notes & instructions
steps.text: This is where you tell Campaignia how to create your story — anything it should know or do.

steps.title: Generate Story
steps.text: Campaignia reads your story and your notes, then compiles the Moments that should be turned into images.

steps.title: Your cast
steps.text: These are the characters in this session.

steps.title: Edit a character
steps.text: Edit how a character looks going forward. Type your instructions in the box above, then Retouch the character to update the reference image.

steps.title: Pick the Moment
steps.text: Select which Moment this visual change takes place. The character looks normal before it, and changed from it onward.

steps.title: Approve the change
steps.text: Approve the change to lock in the new look from the chosen Moment onward.

steps.title: Review before you generate
steps.text: See Campaignia's plan before it generates anything. Every image panel and every bridge between them shows an outline — the facts the narration will cover — so you can fix anything missing or out of order before spending tokens.

steps.title: Edit the plan
steps.text: On each panel, edit the Narrative Outline (the facts to cover), the Narrative Direction (how it's written — tone and pacing), or the Image Prompt (the picture), and add or remove characters and assets. On a phone these collapse into a menu.

steps.title: Style, then generate
steps.text: Set your Art Style and Narrative Style for this session, then Generate Narrative & Images to turn the outline into your Story.

steps.title: Your storyboard
steps.text: Every image in the session lives here, ready to refine.

steps.title: Title image
steps.text: The opening image for your story — usually a wide, distant shot that sets the scene.

steps.title: A panel
steps.text: Each panel is one Moment from your story.

steps.title: Edit prompt
steps.text: Edit the image prompt here, then Regenerate to apply it.

steps.title: Regenerate
steps.text: Makes a fresh image from the prompt.

steps.title: Retouch
steps.text: Keeps the image as is, but lets you change small details.

steps.title: Replace
steps.text: Pull a different image in from your Archive.

steps.title: Lock
steps.text: Keeps this image from being overwritten on a global Regenerate.

steps.title: Archive
steps.text: Sends a copy of this image to your Archive.

steps.title: Cast for this Moment
steps.text: Open these options to add or remove characters and assets for this Moment — just like the Review tab. Make your changes, then Regenerate.

steps.title: Prominence
steps.text: High prominence makes this picture as big as possible when published.

steps.title: Narrative
steps.text: Regenerate the narrative if you do not like it, or simply retype it yourself.

steps.title: Layout
steps.text: Choose how your story is laid out — comic, picture book, or magazine. (Same as the Publish page.)

steps.title: Quick View vs True View
steps.text: Use Quick View to test and tweak quickly; switch to True View for an exact final look. (Same as the Publish page.)

steps.title: Draft or Ready
steps.text: When you mark a session Ready, other members can see it and create their own versions of it.
